statement: The odd-to-odd Juggler starts have natural density 1/4. Equivalently, the starts that admit a uniform one- or two-step FiniteProgress certificate (every even start n ≥ 2, and every odd start whose first image is even) have natural density 3/4. This is the counting corollary |OO(N)-N/4| ≪ N^{5/6} of the ambient odd-input discrepancy bound. It is a density of that uniform short-certificate class, not of all FiniteProgress, not of ReachesOne, and not a Lean counting theorem.

proof_routes.notes: The elementary count uses the classical second-derivative/discrepancy input in this proof. Those external theorem instances are not yet separate ledger nodes.

statement: For a primitive exact threshold cycle S_b, or an actual Juggler cycle with minimum m>1 and maximum M<m^3, let L,o be its period and lower/odd count, T=log 3, Lambda=o log 3-L log 2>0, and A=(log m) exp(-(1-1/L)Lambda)>0. Then Lambda < exp(-A)/A times the finite sum over 0<=i<L of exp(-i T(A+1)/L), and exp(A) A(A+1)Lambda < A+1+L/T. The exact upper unit cells bound each logarithmic defect by 1/(y log y); the sorted grid bounds the total by a geometric sum. Along sequences with log m tending to infinity, log m=o(L), and Lambda log m tending to zero, this yields m(log m)^2 Lambda <= (1+o(1))L/log 3. In the explicitly conditional regime Lambda~c/L and polynomially growing m, this narrows the necessary scale to m(log m)^2<=(1+o(1))L^2/(c log 3). No uniform lower bound of order 1/L for Lambda is asserted. The result also holds for wrong-parity threshold cycles and does not prove a parity obstruction, no-cycle, or a new numerical period bound. The exact finite and scaled scalar inequalities are kernel checked in CubicUpperCells. The asymptotic consequences remain written, so this combined row retains its written-proof tag. Independent human review is not claimed.

Let G(1)=1, G(x)=J(x)-1 for odd x>=3, and G(x)=J(x) for even x. Exact integer square-cell inequalities certify the primitive cycle 13,45,300,17,69,572,23,109,1136,33,188,13, with (L,o,e)=(11,7,4) and maximum 1136<13^3. It is also an R_11 cycle. For any two odd sources >=3, or two positive even sources, G(x')-G(x)=J(x')-J(x). All same-branch higher finite differences on sources >1 therefore agree as well. Even strict nearest-even smooth-gap tests hold for same-parity successor pairs. Hence correct source parity, global rank order and exact within-branch image differences restricted to sources >1 alone cannot exclude cycles: an additive branch constant is lost. Differences involving 1 are excluded because they could anchor the odd-branch constant. This is a cycle of a different map, not a Juggler counterexample. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. The illustrative asymptotic comparison and universal wrong-parity question are not promoted; no new cycle exclusion, floor or period bound follows.

At n = 10^6+1 the run-type 6/5 packing is strictly below the parity RHS on every one of the 141 lengths in E_par(10^6). It certified-excludes the 42 lengths 56347+1054k for k = 0..41 and leaves 99 leftovers. First survivor remains L = 25781 (θ ≈ 2.55e-5 versus packed RHS ≈ 5.89e-4). Dropping one even term (M → ∞) does not change the kill list. Paper A Theorem 4.8. Not a halt theorem.

Conditional cycle-order theorem. Let C be a primitive nontrivial Juggler cycle with minimum m>1, maximum M<m^3, length L and o odd states; set e=L-o. If c_0=m<...<c_(L-1) lists its states, the odd states are exactly those below m^2 and J(c_i)=c_((i+e) mod L). Hence gcd(L,o)=1 and the odd count in the first k steps from m is ceil(k o/L), for 0<=k<=L: the exact ceiling mechanical word. Proof separates odd/even states and images, uses injectivity to eliminate possible floor ties, then ranks the resulting cyclic permutation. A non-mechanical primitive cycle or one with gcd(L,o)>1 must instead have M>=m^3+1. The height hypothesis is essential to this argument; no unconditional Christoffel claim, no parity obstruction, no new period exclusion. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. The illustrative asymptotic comparison and universal wrong-parity question are not promoted; no new cycle exclusion, floor or period bound follows.

For a finite sorted invariant set with rank permutation i->i+b modulo a+b, positive a,b, and chronological return words A,B, inducing on a prefix gives (a-b,b;A,AB) if a>b, or (a,b-a;AB,B) if b>a. Accelerating a=qb+r gives (r,b;A,A^q B), and b=qa+r gives (a,r;AB^q,B); a zero remainder gives the identity on the gcd-sized prefix. Return towers partition all original states, preserving a|A|+b|B|=L and letter counts. Exact parity predicates compose as P_AB(x)=P_A(x) AND P_B(F_A(x)). Therefore the full expanded tower representation retains exactly L original source-parity tests at every stage. For a primitive cycle the terminal single base carries the entire original fixed-point and parity condition. These first returns concern the finite invariant set, not every integer between its extrema. This is elementary symbolic induction with a faithful parity interpretation, not a uniform arithmetic-closure theorem, a lower bound on every possible representation, or a no-cycle proof. The exact subtractive rank first returns and their word statistics are Lean verified in J-cycle-subtractive-return-step; the accelerated full tower partition remains written. No uniform guard compression or no-cycle theorem.

For every odd integer s>=3, take threshold b=s^3 and source x=s^4. The exact threshold map S_b makes the lower-to-lower first-return block s^4 -> s^6 -> s^3, since s^3<=s^4<s^6=b^2<b^3. Both endpoints are odd and the collapsed OE endpoint is exactly x^(3/4)=s^3, but the eliminated E source s^6 is odd; the actual Juggler map there gives s^9. Thus exact collapsed endpoint cells, odd endpoint parity and threshold cuts do not imply the original internal parity guard. This family occurs at unbounded cube thresholds, not every threshold, and its members are blocks rather than closed cycles. It refutes omitting internal parity, not short-word endpoint identities, guarded compression, or any full-cycle assertion. The prescribed power family and all three odd parities are Lean verified by oe_perfect_power and oe_perfect_power_hidden_odd; the threshold placement and the actual image s^9 are Lean verified by thresholdMap_cube_block and floorPower_hidden_odd_block. These are blocks, not cycles.

For positive integer x and O(x)=floor(x^(3/2)), E(x)=floor(sqrt x), chronological OE equals floor(x^(3/4)) exactly. If H=floor(x^(9/8)), then F_OOE(x) is H or H-1, so an odd output equals the largest odd integer at most x^(9/8). For x>=5, 0<=x^(27/32)-F_OOEOE(x)<2; hence an odd output is the odd projection. The same odd-output assertion holds for positive odd sources below 5 by x=1 and x=3 controls. For any fixed word, defining n_j=floor(n_(j-1)^alpha_j), p_j=product alpha up to j, q_j=p_k/p_j, and actual error eps_j=n_(j-1)^alpha_j-n_j, the loss telescopes exactly as x^p_k-n_k=sum_j[(n_j+eps_j)^q_j-n_j^q_j]. If every nonempty proper prefix, 1<=j<k, has p_j>p_k, it is less than 1+sum_(j<k)q_j n_j^(q_j-1). A sum at most 1 therefore suffices for odd projection; each such fixed word eventually satisfies this as x grows. This supplies no uniform word-independent bound and does not establish internal source parity, arbitrary Euclidean endpoint closure, or a no-cycle theorem. OE/OOE integer cells and the OOE odd maximal endpoint are Lean verified in J-cycle-short-return-cells. The OOEOE projection and fixed-word asymptotic transport remain written; no uniform growing-word conclusion.

For a primitive S_b cycle, or an actual Juggler cycle with minimum m>1 and maximum M<m^3, sort its states c_i and set T=log 3, Lambda=o log 3-L log 2>0, v_i=log(log c_i/log m), v_(i+L)=v_i+T and w_i=v_i-iT/L. Then osc(w)<= (1-1/L)Lambda and |w_i|<= (1-1/L)Lambda. The lifted adjacent gaps h_i=v_(i+1)-v_i satisfy range(h)<=Lambda and |h_i-T/L|<=(1-1/L)Lambda. The proof uses nonnegative logarithmic rounding defects summing to Lambda and the coprime rank rotation, with no factor L loss. The bounds do not resolve integer parity or exclude cycles. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. The illustrative asymptotic comparison and universal wrong-parity question are not promoted; no new cycle exclusion, floor or period bound follows.

For a guarded sorted OOE/OE return model with positive counts a,b and least source at least m>=2^24, the first maximal left and right batches have quotient2 and nonzero remainders: a=2b+r,b=2r+s,0<s<r<b. dc_rank_stages proves this from exact guarded rank equations and compiled growth/decrease inequalities, including terminal equality. periodicExtrema_return_model constructs this model for an actual cycle with M<m^3. periodicExtrema_dc_transfers proves that the left steps recycle one seam and the next two right steps genuinely transfer it through C. The broader unguarded threshold-model version remains written; this Lean row states the guarded version.

For the prescribed return C=OOEOOEOE and every integer x>=2^24, 0<=x^(243/256)-F_C(x)<9/8. The kernel-checked seven-tail majorant is 63121/524288<1/8. For integers z>w>=2^24 with d=z-w>=2, 0<=F_C(z)-F_C(w)<(243/256)w^(-13/256)d+9/8<d. No parity hypothesis is needed for this prescribed-map inequality. The compiled even-gap and actual-cycle transfer layers supply its cycle use. Paper A Section3.12 and AppendixF; no no-cycle claim.

Paper A Theorem3.40(i): Every actual Juggler cycle with minimum m>=2^24 and maximum M<m^3 satisfies M<m^3-(1/2)m^(253/128), and m^253<[2(m^3-M)]^128. The compiled companion dc_cycle_gap proves d0=F_OOE(m)-F_OE(sqrt M)>=6 and d0>(26240/59049)m^(13/128). The actual section, guards, forced batches, two genuine transfers, analytic bounds and exact extremal cells are derived internally. Ordinary periodic-orbit and CycleMin wrappers are included. The remaining cubic region and taller cycles remain open; period780239 and descent floor350000000 are unchanged.

On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of length L and oddCount o, the dyadic-cell logarithm bound log z ≤ 2 log y + 2/y unrolls to n · log n · (3^o − 2^L) ≤ L · 3^o (Paper A Theorem 4.4; Lean cycleMin_finance). Every cycle state is at least 12 and the rotated minimum is odd, so the minimum is at least 13 and 13 log 13 > 65/2, hence (65/2)(3^o − 2^L) ≤ L · 3^o for every CycleItinerary (cycle_finance_min_thirteen). This is the whole-cycle financing of the formal expansion 2^L < 3^o by relative floor defects. It is not a halt theorem, not an exclusion of every length, and not the computational 6/5 table used for L ≤ 10^5.

For a finite sequence of even natural gaps d(0),...,d(n), if every step strictly decreases then d(n)+2n<=d(0). If the final gap is positive then 2(n+1)<=d(0). The previous two- and three-transfer bounds are special cases. Every strict transfer remains a hypothesis; no unlimited chain is inferred.

Every nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ≥ 2 is formally expanding. Cycle extrema satisfy the certified parity, order, square-scale, and nested-cell constraints; a minimum-based cycle orientation cannot end in an odd letter. The path from a cycle minimum to any later even state is superquadratic. These are necessary cycle restrictions, not an exclusion of all cycles.

Paper A Appendix E.6, explicit formal witness. For every requested modulus q>0, c=512q-1 and b=c^3 yield two prescribed OOE first-return blocks in the same full cubic threshold band and the same section. The source, first image and endpoint are odd, all six threshold edges and first-return memberships are proved, and the final E-source parities differ. The records agree in source/first-image/endpoint/natural-aggregate residues modulo q, exact first remainder zero, and exact aggregate 2-adic valuation three. No classifier of this record can give both hidden parities correctly, even when supplied the exact common threshold and section boundary. The general positive free-b Taylor construction remains written. These blocks are not asserted periodic points; no impossibility for full absolute-value formulas or cycle-specific guards is claimed. Kernel verified.

For every word pair induced from (OOE,OE) by the two Euclidean substitutions, o(U)e(V)-o(V)e(U)=1 as an integer identity. Each word has coprime odd/even counts. For arbitrary natural section populations a,b, the expanded totals L=a|U|+b|V| and o=a o(U)+b o(V) satisfy gcd(L,o)=gcd(a,b). These count identities preserve the guards in separate actual-return interfaces; they alone do not construct a cycle.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, and every length in [30, 10^5) outside a named list of near-convergents is already excluded, then the period is 84, or belongs to that list, or is at least 10^5. Lean theorem cycle_itinerary_eliahou_leftover: bookkeeping on cycle_itinerary_length_eighty_four_or_ge_eighty_five plus EliahouTable, not a new inequality. This is the Collatz Eliahou leftover shape (period ≥ X, or a named convergent family) on the floor-power map. Paper A prints the floor-10^6 instance as Theorem 4.6; leftover 84 is Appendix A companion. This is not a proof of the finance table, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle exists, there is no period ≤ 25780, and no period ≤ 10^5 outside the 141 near-convergent lengths of ln 2 / ln 3 at the Python floor 10^6 using the length-only parity 6/5 table (Paper A Theorem 4.6). First record survivor is L = 25781. Instantiation of J-cycle-itinerary-eliahou-leftover by the parity finance gap table L ≤ 10^5 and descent floor 10^6. Length 84 is the Lean-named leftover (Appendix A companion) and is computationally already excluded. Lengths 19, 38, 57, and 76 are excluded in Lean at the residual floor 261. This is not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem and not a halt theorem.

For a prescribed word with full ideal exponent 0<p<1 and every proper tail q_j=p/p_j<1, two traces whose sources and proper states are at least m>=1 satisfy 0<=F(z)-F(w)<p*m^(p-1)*(z-w)+K_W(m), where K_W=1+sum(q_j*m^(q_j-1)). The condition 2*p*m^(p-1)+K_W<=2 forces strict contraction on gaps at least two. For p>1/2 and a proper prefix this sufficient certificate requires m>(2p)^(1/(1-p)); hence it cannot hold uniformly at a fixed minimum for a family with p approaching one from below. This is a limitation of the one-sided error estimate, not a counterexample to true paired contraction or a claim that every possible later upper word has these exponents. The exact transported loss, paired bound and necessary finite minimum threshold are kernel checked in ReturnWordLoss, retaining the published ReturnWordBounds namespace for the threshold. The p-to-one asymptotic interpretation remains written, so this combined row retains its written-proof tag. No no-cycle conclusion.

Paper A Theorem3.40(ii): Every actual Juggler cycle with minimum m>=2^128 and maximum M<m^3 satisfies M<m^3-(1/2)m^theta, theta=381/128-3^41/2^65>127/64, also M<m^3-(1/2)m^(127/64) and m^127<[2(m^3-M)]^64. The forced next batch has r=3s+u,0<u<s. The unconditional 65-letter W=D^3C loss is below6/5 and its genuine third transfer forces d0>=8 and d0>(2/5)m^(13/128+1-3^41/2^65). The full actual placement, guards and cell transport are kernel checked; ordinary periodic-orbit and CycleMin wrappers are included. This theorem retains its much larger cutoff and does not exclude all cubic or taller cycles or increase the period/descent floor.

Paper A Proposition E.2. For positive y and y^4<=N<(y+1)^4, let u=isqrt(N), c=u-y^2, d=(N-y^4) div (2y^2), h=min(d,2y). Then 0<=c<=2y and c<=h<=c+2. The exact 0/1/2 correction is recovered by the two adjacent square comparisons (baseline_zero_iff, baseline_one_iff, baseline_two_iff). For odd y, the hidden source u is even iff c is odd (square_guard_iff). With N=x^3 and an odd OE source, this is the exact internal guard. Kernel-verified quantified bounds and recovery; the sharpness example 93->896->29 is separately checked finite arithmetic. No arbitrary-word closure or cycle theorem is asserted.

For every odd integer r>=3, x=r^8+8,u=r^12+12r^4,v=r^18+18r^10+54r^2-1,z=r^9+9r-1 form a genuine parity-valid Juggler OOE block x->u->v->z in threshold band [b,b^3), b=r^8, with x,u,z below b^2 and v above it; max(block)<min(block)^3. Its true suffix quotient is d=floor((u^3-z^4)/(2z^2)); the candidate pure-power replacement is D=floor((x^(9/2)-z^4)/(2z^2)). Exactly D-d is 36r^2 or 36r^2+1. For c=v-z^2 and H=min(D,2z), c=2z-27r^2, H=2z, and H-c=27r^2. Meanwhile floor(x^(9/8))=z+1 and odd projection gives the correct endpoint z. Hence no uniformly bounded additive correction repairs this specified quotient or clipped-displacement substitution. The ideal radicand lies outside the original unit endpoint cell at z, so the example refutes a candidate closure extension rather than the valid one-block normal form. The actual first square remainder is 48r^8+512 and cannot simply be discarded in that extension. These are blocks, not cycles; the family itself has a polynomial-plus-one-carry correction, so no impossibility for general fixed-dimensional data or parity-only formulas is claimed. The exact polynomial Juggler block, the two quotient floors (d=2r^9-27r^2+18r and D=2r^9+9r^2+18r+1, so D-d=36r^2+1), the clipped-error calculation and floor(x^(9/8))=z+1 are Lean verified. No periodic membership is claimed.

Paper A Proposition E.5 and ER1. For an exact first root u=isqrt(x^3)>=3, retained remainder R=x^3-u^2, and validated OE suffix endpoint z, the correction error C-Delta=eta^2(t+2u)/(4z^2) is in [0,5/6). The signed corrected floor q is d or d-1, where d=floor((u^3-z^4)/(2z^2)). corrected_quotient_integer proves q=(isqrt(K^2*x^3)-2z^4) floor-divided by 4z^2, K=2x^3-3R. endpoint_validation certifies z via z^8<=(x^3-R)^3<(z+1)^8; record_initializes checks an independently supplied square/remainder witness. The executable recoverPeak evaluates this integer quotient and the four candidate fourth-power cells; recoverPeak_eq proves exact recovery of v=isqrt(u^3). For odd initial x, both hidden OOE source guards hold iff R is even and recoverPeak is even. Initial record and endpoint validity are explicit, not inferred from a projected candidate. This is a kernel-verified short-word algorithm; the additional OOEOE composition remains written, and no arbitrary-word closure or speedup is claimed.

Paper A Theorem E.4. For X(r)=r^8+8 and odd parameters r>=3, the exact three-step Juggler image is r^9+9r-1. A family transition r->s is equivalent to s^8+9=r^9+9r and forces r=1 modulo48. Between continuing sources, nu2(s-1)=nu2(r-1)-2. For a finite actual J^3 chain of k transitions through odd parameters >=3, k<=(nu2(r0-1)-2)/2 with natural-number subtraction and division; this is max(0,floor((nu2(r0-1)-2)/2)) in integer notation. No valuation drop is assumed after the final destination. ooeFamily_no_infinite_juggler_chain excludes an infinite exact family chain. These are direct actual-Juggler wrappers, not merely an assumed polynomial recurrence. The supplementary 3-adic identity is written and six terminating sample traces are computations. No universal family termination, general escape exclusion, or no-cycle theorem follows.

For every even Q>=2 put c=Q-1 and choose a positive integer b=3 mod4 with b^2>504c^5. For d=1,-c define t_d=b^4+4d, x_d=t_d^2, u_d=t_d^3, V_d=b^18+18db^14+126d^2b^10+420d^3b^6+630d^4b^2 and Z_d=b^9+9db^5+(45d^2b-1)/2. Exact prescribed OOE traces have second images v_1=V_1 and v_-c=V_-c-1 and endpoints Z_d. Both first remainders x_d^3-u_d^2 equal zero. Both x_d,u_d,Z_d are odd, but v_1 is odd and v_-c is even, so precisely the negative-d guard holds. The traces are first returns to the same integer section [B,Z_1+1), B=t_-c^2, of the same threshold map on [B,B^3), with both intermediate states outside that section and correct OOE threshold placement. Their x,u,Z and endpoint-aggregate x^9-Z^8 residues agree modulo Q, and both aggregate 2-adic valuations equal 3. Taking Q an even multiple of any fixed finite collection of residue moduli proves that no function of just those residues, the exact first remainder, aggregate valuation, word and common full threshold/section can recognize every such guard. This refutes that precise fixed-residue summary class on the geometric return domain, not absolute-value quotient formulas, a fixed number of unbounded registers, or a cycle-selected representation. Periodic membership of these blocks is not asserted. The general positive-b construction is a written proof. A fully quantified explicit every-modulus subfamily is Lean verified in J-cycle-fixed-residue-witness. No periodicity or global no-cycle claim.

Paper A Proposition E.3, formal polynomial-block subset. For every odd r>=3, x=r^8+8,u=r^12+12r^4,v=r^18+18r^10+54r^2-1,z=r^9+9r-1 satisfy all three adjacent-square cells, x,u,z odd and v even, and the actual Juggler steps x->u->v->z. The direct iterate-three identity is proved. Kernel verified; this row does not cover the real-power quotient substitution estimates or assert a closed orbit.

The length-only parity 6/5 table at the published floor N_0 = 10^6 excludes every cycle length L ≤ 25780 and every L ≤ 10^5 outside 141 near-convergent lengths. First survivor L = 25781 with n_max^par = 26254995; n_max^par(1054) = 788014. No comparison is uncertain. SHA-256 of the length list is dd71aa1527656ba51cb031bafa5497f7bfdbbc43151ffba2c595793326bf7944. This is not the crude table at floor 2·10^6 (same prefix, weaker inequality). Not a halt theorem and not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem.

Paper A Theorem 3.39. For every actual cycle with attained minimum m>=5 and maximum M<m^3, t=isqrt(M) and z=F_OOE(m) satisfy t^3+2<=[z(z-2)]^2 and M+2<=(t+1)^2 (cycleMin_exact_return_seam). The periodic E-image section is exactly C intersect [m,O(m)); its extrema return images have a strict odd gap, derived from actual periodicity and injectivity rather than assumed. For m>=7, m^15<(m^3-M)^8 (cycleMin_height_strip), equivalently M<m^3-m^(15/8); the all-states version is cycleMin_all_states_height_strip. Every threshold cycle in the complementary top strip has a wrong-parity state (threshold_cycle_wrong_parity). Exact OE/OOE cells identify the odd endpoint z. The sharper fractional bound for t, maximum-odd-integer ceiling restatement, and full rank adjacency are separately written consequences. The remaining cubic region, tall cycles and global no-cycle remain unexcluded; the period floor is unchanged. Kernel verified from actual periodic-orbit and CycleMin hypotheses.

Paper A Appendix E.1, formal subset. The prescribed OE return equals y iff y^4<=x^3<(y+1)^4. Every prescribed OOE return v satisfies v^8<=x^9<(v+2)^8; relative to an eighth-root cell y it is y or y-1. If v is odd, it is the greatest odd integer whose eighth power is at most x^9. The family s^4->s^6->s^3 has all three states odd when s is odd, so endpoint parities do not imply the hidden E guard. Actual OE/OOE composition bridges retain every source-parity premise. Kernel verified; no arbitrary-root or OOEOE projection theorem is claimed by this row.

Paper A Appendix E.2, formal core. For rankStep(a,b,i)=i+b when i<a and i-a otherwise, a>b gives the first return on [0,a) as rankStep(a-b,b), in one or two iterations with every earlier positive iterate outside. For b>a the first return on [0,b) is rankStep(a,b-a); equal counts give a two-step identity. Weighted word lengths and O/E statistics are preserved by A,AB or AB,B substitution. Kernel-verified return iterates and first-visit properties; full accelerated towers and their global partition remain written.

Every actual positive periodic orbit with minimum m>=3, attained maximum M<m^3 and all states in [m,M] supplies a primitive terminal two-base section {m,v}. The supplied period need not be least. The original adjacent pair follows induced words U,V with U(m)=v and V(v)=m, and guarded factors UV=P OE Q, VU=P EO Q. Their common prefix reaches the globally adjacent largest odd/smallest even pair (h,s), with O(h)=M and E(s)=m. The common suffix returns (floor(sqrt M),O(m)) to (m,v), and 0<O(m)-floor(sqrt M)<s-h. The periodic-set interface explicitly requires connectedness; the ordinary-orbit interface derives it. Primitive termination, original-set adjacency, exact cut identification and every guard are kernel checked. No contraction of the complete prefix/mixed/suffix passage or no-cycle conclusion is asserted. The stronger TerminalOrbitCut interface is indexed by the same PeriodicOrbitModel used for charge: terminal word lengths sum to its true least period, and odd/even totals equal the parity-filter cardinalities of its sorted states.

For a fixed integer b>=3, all primitive cycles of the size-switched threshold map S_b have the same period L, branch counts (o,e), and minimum-based ceiling mechanical word. If there are t cycles, they interlace: each occupies one rank residue class modulo t in the sorted union of all periodic points. Proof: on that finite invariant union, branch image separation and injectivity give rank addition by E, the total upper-branch count; t=gcd(N,E), L=N/t, e=E/t. No uniqueness, uniform wrong-parity intersection or actual Juggler cycle exclusion follows. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. The illustrative asymptotic comparison and universal wrong-parity question are not promoted; no new cycle exclusion, floor or period bound follows.

For each integer b>=3, the size-switched map S_b on integers b<=x<b^3 uses floor(sqrt(x^3)) for x<b^2 and floor(sqrt(x)) otherwise. This finite interval is invariant and S_b has no fixed point, so it has a primitive cycle of length at least two at arbitrarily large minima. Its cycles have the separated-image rank rotation, coprime branch counts and ceiling mechanical words; 3^o>2^L. S_b is not Juggler: a full cycle is a Juggler cycle iff every low state is odd and every high state even. This parity compatibility is not established, and the construction refutes only attempts to get no-cycle from the listed parity-relaxed properties alone. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. The illustrative asymptotic comparison and universal wrong-parity question are not promoted; no new cycle exclusion, floor or period bound follows.

If a Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ends with r ≥ 1 even letters, the state immediately before that trailing even run is strictly less than (n+1)^{2^r}. The case r = 1 is the last-even one-step preimage; r = 2 is the two-even bound of Paper A Lemma 3.5 on OOOOEE; r = 3 is the three-even bound for OOOOOOEEE. Lean theorem cycle_trailing_evens_lt. This is a one-step-preimage identity, not a leftover exclusion and not a halt theorem.

For every odd integer b>=3, let D_b consist of odd integers in [b,b^2] and even integers in [b^2+1,b^3-1], and let P_b(z) be its largest element <=z for b<=z<=b^3. Define R_b(x)=P_b(x^(3/2)) on odd x and P_b(sqrt x) on even x. This finite map has no fixed point and has a nontrivial cycle; every edge has R_b(x) in {J(x),J(x)-1}. The parity layer's surviving lengths are exactly a one-sided Bohr set with a window linear in L, and its gaps are BETA's Ostrowski denominators. THE CHARACTERISATION. With g(L) = o_min(L) log2(3) - L the walk gap, a cycle needs 3^o > 2^L so only g > 0 matters, and the finance bound (6/5) L 3^o/(3^o - 2^L) is (6/5) L/(1 - 2^(-g)), which blows up as g -> 0. So a length survives a floor exactly when its gap is small RELATIVE to its length: survivors = { L : 0 < g(L) < kappa L }. Measured at floor 1e6 over l_max = 200000, the largest g/L among survivors is 4.635150e-08 and the smallest among non-survivors is 4.647621e-08, so a single threshold separates them and misclassifies NONE of the 199424 lengths with g > 0. THE WINDOW SCALES AS 1/(n0 ln n0): kappa n0 ln n0 reads 0.6412, 0.6241, 0.6390, 0.6585, 0.5453 at floors 1e6, 1e7, 26254995, 68000000, 1e8, flat to about ten percent over two decades. THE GAPS ARE OSTROWSKI DENOMINATORS: consecutive survivors at floor 1e6 differ by 84, 485, 401, 569, 1054, 317 -- 268, 132, 105, 24, 23, 23 times -- every one a convergent or semiconvergent denominator of BETA, which is the three-distance theorem for a Bohr set. 401 and 317 are least-peak staircase jumps and 569 and 1054 are cycle record lengths, so this is the skeleton of J-staircase-and-cycle-records-split-betas-semiconvergents seen from the floor side. WHAT THE LEFTOVERS ARE NOT, and this corrects the obvious guess: they are not the semiconvergents. Of 576 survivors at floor 1e6 only 3 are semiconvergents and 8 are multiples of one; 565 are neither. The semiconvergents are the RECORD-SETTERS of the one-sided approximation, which is why one of them is the FIRST survivor at each floor, not why the set is what it is. WHERE THE CUTOFF MOVES. First exception by floor: 25781 at 1e6 and 1e7; 50508 at 26254995 through 1e8; 101016 at 162848325; 176251 at 3.5e8; and none below 300000 at 1044093214. The floors that move it are n_max^par of the length being killed -- 26254995 for 25781, confirming J-residual-floor-twenty-six-million's claim that it is the cheapest floor moving the Theorem 4.6 cutoff, then 162848325 for 50508 and 1044093214 for 176251. AN OBSERVATION, NOT A CRITICISM: the parked 5.54e8 leaves the parity first exception at 176251, the same as the current N_0 = 3.5e8; it is CONDITIONAL_FLOOR in paper_a_audit and DK_BREAKEVEN_FLOOR in the visualization layer, so it targets the Denjoy-Koksma competition rather than the parity layer, and nothing here bears on whether it is the right floor for that. Machinery: parity_leftover_window. No bound moves, no floor is raised, and this is not a halt theorem. PLACED IN PAPER A as Remark 5.13, and the containment turns out to be Paper A's own theorem rather than an import. Theorem 4.10 states n log n min(Lambda,1) <= 2L, so a cycle with minimum n >= N_0 survives a floor only if 0 < Lambda(L) <= 2L/(N_0 log N_0) -- the positivity being the 3^o > 2^L that makes the finance inequality meaningful at all. That is the Bohr condition, PROVED, with crude constant 2; only the sharp constant is measured, and in Paper A's normalisation Lambda = o log 3 - L log 2 it fits to 0.4445, 0.4326, 0.4429, 0.4564, 0.3779 at N_0 = 1e6, 1e7, 26254995, 68000000, 1e8, so the parity layer of Section 5.7 is about 4.5 times sharper than Theorem 4.10's crude form. WHAT IT ADDS TO SECTION 5.8. Proposition 5.12 gives the fan as an arithmetic progression of 56 terms ending on a convergent and then states its own limitation: 'no all-index transition theorem is asserted: excluding a fan member also requires ruling out intervening non-fan lengths.' The Bohr set is what those intervening lengths are, so the caveat becomes an explicit finite set at each floor rather than an open worry. The remark also corrects the natural misreading of Proposition 5.12 -- the survivors are NOT the fan; of 576 at N_0 = 1e6 only three are semiconvergents and eight are multiples, and the fan members are the record-setters, which is why one is always the FIRST survivor and why the frontier climbs the fan. Nothing in the remark is a new exclusion and no bound moves; Paper A's headline period bound 780239 is unchanged and was already in the deposited version 1.0.0.
